arxiv-1911-11801.title: Ramsey interferometry with generalized one-axis twisting echoes
arxiv-1911-11801.creator: Marius Schulte, Victor J. Martínez-Lahuerta, Maja S. Scharnagl, Klemens Hammerer
arxiv-1911-11801.description: Abstract We consider a large class of Ramsey interferometry protocols which are enhanced by squeezing and un-squeezing operations before and after a phase signal is imprinted on the collective spin of N N particles. We report an analytical optimization for any given particle number and strengths of (un-)squeezing.

arxiv-2205-09755.title: Anisotropy of Halo Main Sequence Turnoff Stars Measured with New MMT Radial Velocities and Gaia Proper Motions Facilities: MMT (Hectospec Spectrograph), Gaia
arxiv-2205-09755.creator: Charles King III, Warren R. Brown, Margaret J. Geller, Scott J. Kenyon
arxiv-2205-09755.description: Abstract We measure the anisotropy of the Milky Way stellar halo traced by a dense sample of 18 < r < 21 18<r<21 mag F-type main sequence turnoff stars using Gaia eDR3 proper motions and new radial velocity measurements published here.

arxiv-2303-17012.title: Advances in apparent conceptual physics reasoning in GPT-4
arxiv-2303-17012.creator: Colin G. West 1
arxiv-2303-17012.description: Abstract ChatGPT is an interface built on a large language model trained on an enormous corpus of human text to emulate human conversation. Despite ChatGPT’s lack of any explicit programming regarding the laws of physics, recent work has demonstrated that the version built on GPT-3.

arxiv-2309-05471.title: Electron and photon energy calibration with the ATLAS detector using LHC Run 2 data
arxiv-2309-05471.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . This paper presents the electron and photon energy calibration obtained with the ATLAS detector using 140 fb -1 of LHC proton–proton collision data recorded at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV between 2015 and 2018. Methods for the measurement of electron and photon energies are outlined, along with the current knowledge of the passive material in front of the ATLAS electromagnetic calorimeter. The energy calibration steps are discussed in detail, with emphasis on the improvements introduced in this paper.

arxiv-2403-02585.title: High-Rate 16 16 -node quantum access network based on passive optical network
arxiv-2403-02585.creator: Yan Pan, Yiming Bian, Yang Li, Xuesong Xu, Li Ma, Heng Wang, Yujie Luo, Jiayi Dou, Yaodi Pi, Jie Yang, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Stefano Pirandola, Yichen Zhang, Bingjie Xu
arxiv-2403-02585.description: Abstract Quantum key distribution can provide information-theoretical secure communication, which is now heading towards building the quantum secure network for real-world applications. In most built quantum secure networks, point-to-multipoint (PTMP) topology is one of the most popular schemes, especially for quantum access networks.

arxiv-2407-13187.title: Growth and shrinkage of tissue sheets on substrates: buds, buckles, and pores
arxiv-2407-13187.creator: Hiroshi Noguchi, Jens Elgeti
arxiv-2407-13187.description: Abstract Many tissues take the form of thin sheets, being only a single cell thick, but millions of cells wide. These tissue sheets can bend and buckle in the third dimension. In this work, we investigated the growth and shrinkage of suspended and supported tissue sheets using particle-based simulations.

arxiv-2410-23786.title: Conformal inference for cell type annotation with graph-structured constraints
arxiv-2410-23786.creator: Daniela Corbetta, Livio Finos, Ludwig Geistlinger, Davide Risso
arxiv-2410-23786.description: Abstract Conformal inference is a method that provides prediction sets for machine learning models, operating independently of the underlying distributional assumptions and relying solely on the exchangeability of training and test data. Despite its wide applicability and popularity, its application in graph-structured problems remains underexplored.

arxiv-2511-11488.title: Stability conditions of the N N -model with a waiting time dependent threshold on the diagonal
arxiv-2511-11488.creator: Sanne van Kempen, Elene Anton, Fiona Sloothaak
arxiv-2511-11488.description: Abstract We consider the N N -model queueing system with a waiting time dependent threshold on the diagonal: the service discipline is First–Come–First–Served, but type-1 jobs can only be served by server 2 if their waiting time exceeds a deterministic threshold.

arxiv-2601-16203.title: Cyclic sunspot activity during the first millennium CE as reconstructed from radiocarbon
arxiv-2601-16203.creator: I. Usoskin ,, S.K. Solanki, N.A. Krivova, T. Chatzistergos
arxiv-2601-16203.description: Abstract Context. Solar activity, dominated by the 11-year cyclic evolution, has been observed directly since 1610 CE. Before that, indirect cosmogenic proxy data are used to reconstruct it over millennia. Recently, the precision of radiocarbon Δ 14 \Delta^{14} C measurements has improved sufficiently to allow reconstructing cyclic solar activity over millennia. Aims.

arxiv-2602-18350.title: Quantum-enhanced satellite image classification
arxiv-2602-18350.creator: Qi Zhang, Anton Simen, Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gabriel Alvarado Barrios, Paolo A. Erdman, Enrique Solano, Aaron C. Kemp, Vincent Beltrani, Vedangi Pathak, Hamed Mohammadbagherpoor
arxiv-2602-18350.description: Abstract We demonstrate the application of a quantum feature extraction method to enhance multi-class image classification for space applications. By harnessing the dynamics of many-body spin Hamiltonians, the method generates expressive quantum features that, when combined with classical processing, lead to quantum-enhanced classification accuracy.

pmc-13002527.description: Corresponding AuthorKey words: arrhythmias, cilostazol, conduction system Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 (PDE3) inhibitor, is widely recognized for its vascular and antiplatelet effects. pmc-13593773.title: Warmth and competence in affective companion virtual humans: differential effects on behavioral intention via hedonic benefits
pmc-13593773.creator: Ting Zhang
pmc-13593773.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Generation Z increasingly engages with affective companion virtual humans not as tools but as partners. However, it remains unclear how social perceptions—specifically warmth and competence—privacy-related attitudes jointly influence their behavioral intention, and whether hedonic benefits mediate these effects. Drawing on the hedonic motivation system acceptance model and the stereotype content model, this study proposes an integrated model linking perceived warmth, perceived competence, perceived privacy risk and privacy cynicism to behavioral intention toward affective companion virtual humans, with hedonic benefits as a mediator.
